title: Finite Rees module of ideal-power cohomology for proper algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Work with module sheaves on the small etale ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F$ be coherent: it is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and on every Noetherian affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ it is associated to a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $J=I\mathcal O_X$ and let $J^rF\subseteq F$ be the submodule locally generated by products of $r$ local sections of $J$ and one of $F$, with $J^0F=F$. Write $\iota_r:J^rF\hookrightarrow F$ for inclusion. Fix $q\geq0$ and put $M_r=H^q(X,J^rF)$, the right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with $A$-action induced by $f^\sharp$. Set $B=\mathcal R_A(I)=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}I^kt^k\subseteq A[t]$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra]. For $k,r\geq0$ and $a\in I^k$, multiplication defines an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\lambda_{k,r}(a):J^rF\to J^{r+k}F$ characterized, on every small etale chart $U\to X$ and section $s\in(J^rF)(U)$, by
$$\iota_{r+k}(\lambda_{k,r}(a)(s))=f^\sharp(a)|_U\,\iota_r(s).$$
Its induced cohomology map $L(k,r,a)=H^q(X,\lambda_{k,r}(a)):M_r\to M_{r+k}$ is $A$-linear, and $L(0,r,a)(x)=ax$ for every $a\in A$. The additive direct sum $M=\bigoplus_{r\geq0}M_r$ is a finitely generated $B$-module under the convolution action
$$\left(\sum_k a_kt^k\right)(x_r)_r=\left(\sum_{k+r=d}L(k,r,a_k)(x_r)\right)_{d\geq0},$$
where both inputs have finite support. In particular the degree-zero $A$-action of this $B$-module is the specified $A$-action on each $M_r$.

source.place: Tag 08AW, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F; the preceding paragraph defines the ideal-power submodules. The action and its degree-zero normalization are the natural graded action used in the lemma.

proof.text: For each $r$, $J^rF$ is the image of $\bigoplus_{a\in I^r}F\to F$, $(s_a)\mapsto\sum_a f^\sharp(a)s_a$: expanding the local generators of $J$ proves this equality, including $r=0$. These are maps of module sheaves. The source direct sum is quasi-coherent, so the image is quasi-coherent by lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits. The same node makes $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_rJ^rF$ quasi-coherent. On an affine etale chart the quasi-coherent equivalence identifies these images with the usual module images; this also identifies restrictions with ideal-power products.

source.place: Tag 08AW, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, proof; corrected use of the pulled-back Rees algebra, without assuming flatness.

proof.text: If $a\in I^k$, multiplying a local generator of $J^rF$ by $f^\sharp(a)$ gives a section of $J^{r+k}F$, by $I^kI^r=I^{k+r}$. Thus multiplication restricts uniquely to $\lambda_{k,r}(a)$, and satisfies the displayed inclusion formula; injectivity of the inclusions proves uniqueness. On sections, addition of coefficients gives addition of these maps, their composites multiply coefficients, and $\lambda_{0,r}(1)=\mathrm{id}$. Multiplication by $a\in A$ in degree zero is the ordinary scalar endomorphism. These maps commute with every module scalar endomorphism. The right-derived universal delta-functor theorem makes cohomology additive; its functoriality preserves these equalities; consequently $L(k,r,a)$ is $A$-linear and $L(0,r,a)(x)=ax$.

source.place: Tag 08AW, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, proof; corrected use of the pulled-back Rees algebra, without assuming flatness.

proof.text: Give $\mathcal G$ its action by $\mathcal B=f^*\widetilde B=\bigoplus_kf^*\widetilde{I^kt^k}$ (the tensor pullback is a left adjoint, so it preserves direct sums; maps out of it are given by the adjunction and its local tensors): on local tensors in degree $k$ set $(c\otimes at^k)s=c\lambda_{k,r}(a)(s)$. The balancing relation follows from $\lambda_{k,r}(ba)=f^\sharp(b)\lambda_{k,r}(a)$ for $b\in A$; the preceding multiplication identities give the algebra-module unit and associativity laws. Local generators of $F$ exist: for an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, the composite to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally of finite type by the chart test defining finite type of $f$, and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian, so $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally Noetherian; on its affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ with $R_i$ Noetherian, which are again etale charts, coherence and the quasi-coherent equivalence make $F$ associated to a finitely generated $R_i$-module. Choose such local generators $s_1,\ldots,s_h$ of $F$, all in degree zero. By step 1, every section of $J^rF$ is locally a sum $\sum_j f^\sharp(a_j)u_j$ with $a_j\in I^r$, $u_j\in F$; after writing $u_j=\sum_i c_{ji}s_i$, this becomes $\sum_i(\sum_j c_{ji}\otimes a_jt^r)s_i$. Hence $\mathcal G$ is finite type over $\mathcal B$, with these same degree-zero generators. This uses the pulled-back algebra, not an identification with $\bigoplus J^k$.

source.place: Tag 08AW, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, proof; corrected use of the pulled-back Rees algebra, without assuming flatness.

proof.text: Noetherianity says $I$ has finitely many generators. By prop-nagata-rees-finite-generation, their degree-one monomials generate $B$ over its degree-zero piece, which is $A$ since $I^0=A$. Thus $B$ is finite type over $A$. Apply lem-sfb-space-graded-cohomology-finite to $\mathcal G$, using properness and the preceding quasi-coherence and finite-type checks. Its convolution formula is exactly the formula in the statement, since multiplication by $at^k$ on the $r$th piece is $\lambda_{k,r}(a)$. This proves finiteness for the specified action; the degree-zero normalization is step 2.
